contentCheck.notes: Two crops cover parts (a)-(c) with the ionization-energy table and parts (d)-(f) with the Lewis-structure boxes; both match page context.

primary.evidence: Must write the gas-phase equation F(g) -> F+(g) + e- that defines the first ionization energy.
Must account for F having a higher first ionization energy than O, discussing both atoms.

supporting.evidence: Explanation requires the greater nuclear charge of F with valence electrons in the same shell, giving stronger attraction for the removed electron.

primary.evidence: Must predict whether the Xe first ionization energy is greater or less than that of F and justify.

supporting.evidence: Justification rests on Xe valence electrons being much farther from the nucleus and more shielded than those of F.

primary.evidence: Must draw complete Lewis diagrams for XeO3 and XeF4, counting valence electrons and placing lone pairs on Xe with an expanded octet.
Must name the shape of XeO3 from the Lewis diagram drawn in (d).

supporting.evidence: Must count four electron domains on Xe (three bonds and one lone pair) to get trigonal pyramidal rather than trigonal planar.

primary.evidence: Must state the hybridization of the Xe valence orbitals in XeF4.

supporting.evidence: Must count six electron domains on Xe (four bonds and two lone pairs) to assign the hybridization.

primary.evidence: Must predict and justify whether XeO3 is polar.

supporting.evidence: Justification depends on the trigonal pyramidal shape, whose Xe-O bond dipoles do not cancel.

uncertainty: Part (e)(ii) requires d-orbital (sp3d2) hybridization, which the current CED does not assess; tagged hybridization anyway.
